text: Real Lex/Yacc execution with visual explanations of compiler concepts.

Project evidence: README.md; frontend/src/App.jsx; frontend/src/components/OutputPanel/OutputPanel.jsx. The screenshot shows the bundled calculator running successfully with stdin 3 + 5 * 2 followed by a newline and stdout 13.

Lexora brings source editing,
native compilation, and compiler
analysis into one browser workspace.
Students compile selected Lex and Yacc specifications using Flex, Bison, and GCC.
A built-in analyzer explains supported input through syntax trees, symbols, and intermediate code.

The compilation process is
difficult to understand when
its intermediate steps
remain hidden.
Students manage separate files and commands to generate, compile, and execute a lexer or parser.
Program output alone does not explain syntax structure, symbol scope, or intermediate code.

These are the teaching and workflow problems the project addresses. They do not represent measured findings from a formal user study. Project evidence: README.md; frontend/src/App.jsx; frontend/src/components/OutputPanel/OutputPanel.jsx.
Students can edit specifications, select targets, and supply program input.
The backend generates C sources, builds an executable, and captures its output.
Visual views connect tokens and syntax structure with symbols and intermediate code.
Browser drafts, examples, and file downloads help students continue their work.
Project evidence: README.md; frontend/src/App.jsx; frontend/src/components/OutputPanel/OutputPanel.jsx. Educational analysis covers the built-in language subset.
Lexora applies established compiler methods through an integrated teaching interface.

The backend aligns parser-header references and regenerates the scanner before GCC runs.

Project evidence: backend/services/compiler.js; backend/services/wslRunner.js; backend/routes/compile.js; backend/middleware/validator.js. Actual combined-mode order: flex lex.l; bison -d parser.y; normalize generated-header references; regenerate scanner; gcc -o compiler lex.yy.c parser.tab.c -lfl -lm; ./compiler < input.txt. Lex Only skips Bison. Yacc Only skips Flex and requires its own yylex and main.
The built-in parser groups multiplication before addition and constructs an abstract syntax tree.
The analyzer also derives scoped symbols, three-address code, optimization results, and basic blocks.
Educational analysis uses Lexora’s supported C subset. Native execution follows the submitted specifications.

Constant folding evaluates arithmetic.
Constant propagation substitutes known values.

Project evidence: backend/services/inputAnalysis.js; backend/services/astGenerator.js; backend/services/semanticAnalyzer.js; backend/services/tacGenerator.js; backend/services/optimizer.js; backend/services/basicBlocks.js. Observed analyzeInput("int x = 2 + 3 * 4;"): AST declaration x:int with addition of 2 and multiplication 3*4. Symbol x global, declared true. TAC and optimized TAC shown exactly. Three assignments remain, so no instruction-count or speed claim applies.
A basic block contains consecutive instructions with no internal branch.
Lexora identifies block leaders and records the successor relationships in the original TAC.

B1: Test condition
x = 1
t1 = x < 3
ifFalse t1 goto L1

B2: Execute body
t2 = x + 1
x = t2

Project evidence: backend/services/inputAnalysis.js; backend/services/astGenerator.js; backend/services/semanticAnalyzer.js; backend/services/tacGenerator.js; backend/services/optimizer.js; backend/services/basicBlocks.js. Observed analyzeInput("int x = 1; if (x < 3) { x = x + 1; }"): B1 x=1, t1=x<3, ifFalse t1 goto L1; B2 t2=x+1, x=t2; B3 L1:. Successors: B1 to B2 and B3, B2 to B3. These blocks use original TAC.
Flex generates the scanner, Bison generates the parser, and GCC builds the program that prints the result.
The bundled calculator expects a newline after each expression.

Project evidence: backend/services/compiler.js; backend/services/wslRunner.js; backend/routes/compile.js; backend/middleware/validator.js. The bundled calculator was executed through the current backend and through the UI. Input was exactly "3 + 5 * 2\n". Observed stdout was "13\n" with successful Flex, Bison, GCC and execution stages. The grammar uses EOL to finish an expression.
Lexora supports selected .l and .y targets and an educational subset of C.
The analyzer currently excludes arrays, structures, pointer declarations, and several other C constructs.
Language and project-file support can expand beyond the current teaching subset.
Public execution would require isolated workers with restricted filesystem and network access.
